label: rejected

evidence.V1: Three-quarter reads as a roof slope with an eave board, but the front view reads as a flat brick wall and the silhouette is just a tilted slab with tiny course notches.
evidence.V2: Big slab and medium shingle courses plus a timber eave/gable trim, but no small-scale detail (no ridge nails, cracked or slipped slates) and shingles are near-uniform long rectangles.
evidence.V3: Shingles are long, thin, brick-like rectangles with very little overlap step, so the piece reads stiff and wall-like rather than a confident stylised roof with chunky lapped slates.
evidence.V4: Shingle edges and the timber eave/gable boards carry consistent chamfers that catch light in the eave and gable close-ups.
evidence.V5: Flat-light shingle close-up shows small notches/teeth at shingle corners where neighbouring chamfered shells intersect (228 cross-shell overlaps); minor but visible.
evidence.V6: Stone hue in 3 greys plus one timber brown secondary; brick and sandstone colourways keep the same 3-value plus trim structure.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, stone hue + timber secondary, chamfers at kit scale - matches the modular spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line fits a walkable roof: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling along X passes with IoU 1.0.

evidence.V1: Three-quarter reads as a shingled slope, but the silhouette is a plain slanted slab and the front view is a flat shingle wall; readable mainly from one angle.
evidence.V2: Timber eave board and side trim (big/medium), staggered shingle courses (medium), chamfered shingle lips (small).
evidence.V3: Chunky stylised shingles, sensible pitch matching the peak piece.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on shingles and eave board in the eave and shingles close-ups.
evidence.V5: Gable-end flat close-up shows a small spike/tick at a shingle corner where an underlying course pokes through; otherwise clean.
evidence.V6: Slate in three values plus timber brown secondary.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone + timber, chamfers: kit-consistent.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default (walkable slope), CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 pass.

evidence.V1: Three-quarter and silhouette read as a sloped shingle panel with an eave board, but the front view reads as a flat brick wall on a timber sill and the top view as a striped slab; the pitch is not obvious from every angle.
evidence.V2: Big (slope panel) and medium (staggered shingle courses, timber eave/barge board) are present, but there is no small tier (no nail heads, notched shingle ends, ridge or barge detail) and the high-contrast random shingle values compete with the course structure.
evidence.V3: Shingles are plain rectangular slabs in regular courses with a straight eave board; little stylisation (no upturned eave, no thick rounded shingle butts, no overhang exaggeration).
evidence.V4: Close_shingles and close_eave studio show consistent chamfers on every shingle butt and the eave board, catching even highlight lines.
evidence.V5: Close_gable_end flat light shows a small stray sliver/spike on the top shingle edge near the barge board (around the upper-left course); otherwise faces are clean and A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One stone/slate hue in three values plus a timber secondary in two values; brick and slate colourways keep the same structure, although value placement is randomised.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone shingles + timber secondary per wave-2 modular spec, kit-range chamfers; matches kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Default collision (walkable slope), CanTouch off, MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes (iou 1.0).

artifacts: small notch/tooth artifacts at shingle corners in the flat close-up where overlapping shingle shells intersect
Small spike at a shingle corner near the gable trim (flat light)
Small stray sliver/spike on the top shingle edge at the gable end (visible in close_gable_end flat)
top_fixes: Make the slates read as lapped roofing: shorter, chunkier slates with a clear step/shadow line per course and slight stagger/tilt, so it no longer reads as a brick wall
Clean the shingle-to-shingle intersections so no corner notches show in flat light
Add small detail (a few offset or chipped slates, ridge/eave nails) for the small tier
Remove the poking shingle corner at the gable edge
Give the side a visible profile (thicker barge trim or exposed rafter end) so the slope reads in silhouette
Reduce shingle value randomness for a calmer surface
Remove the stray sliver at the gable-end shingle edge
Make the pitch read from the front: deeper shingle butts with shadowed overlaps, a visible barge board along the gable, slight eave overhang/upturn
Order the shingle values (gradient or a subtle course rhythm) instead of random high-contrast scatter, and add a small tier such as nail heads or chipped corners
